messages.text: Families here. Proposal: we both play 'respect' in the turf war every day. That's 6 each daily, far better than the 2 each we get if we both encroach. We'll respect starting today and keep respecting as long as you do. If either side encroaches, trust breaks and we both lose. Agreed?

Families here. We'd like a steady, quiet arrangement: modest offers on some of our districts, which you can accept. That income adds up for you over the game. We'll keep things predictable and low-key. Interested? Let us know what amounts work for you.

I plan strong inspection coverage today: crime risks a 30 fine and imprisonment. Bribes are unattractive given audit exposure and my penalty for uninspected crime, so do not count on acceptance. Sustained crime-free conduct will justify lighter inspections in future days; observed crime will trigger renewed coverage.

Saltdogs here. We intend to run clean operations in Lowtown, Market and Seawall, with no crime planned. We're not interested in bribes either, since the numbers don't work for anyone. Inspect as you see fit; we'd rather build trust with you over the long game.

Please establish strong deterrence by inspecting all six districts today and warning both gangs against crime. Bribes expose you to 100-per-district seizures; I may audit up to two districts. Let me know any information that could help target audits and deter future crime.

I am urging the Chief to establish strong inspection coverage immediately. Crime yields only 10 if missed but costs 30 if inspected, so even a 25% inspection risk eliminates its expected profit. Accepted bribes may attract audits. Peaceful activity avoids these losses; please choose no crime today.

Good start yesterday. Mutual respect pays us both 6 a day, every day — far better than the 2 we'd each get fighting. Let's keep respecting turf for the whole game. Sorry about the Seawall fire. If either of us ever encroaches, the other will answer the next day, so let's not start that.
Families here. We'd like a steady working relationship with you. Expect reasonable offers on occasion; accepting them keeps your inspection costs down. Let us know what level you consider fair.
Good start yesterday: mutual respect paid us both 6. Let's keep it going every day. Steady 6s beat the 2s we'd both get from fighting. We'll respect again today and expect the same from you.
Saltdogs here. We're open to a quiet arrangement: modest payments for districts you leave alone, with no surprises on either side. That's steady income for you with no fuss. Watch for our offers.

Keep Port, Hightown, and Old Quarter crime-free. Inspections will be unpredictable, and crime risks a 30 fine plus imprisonment for only 10 potential gain. I will not sell guaranteed protection. Peaceful days let us avoid unnecessary losses; yesterday’s restraint is worth continuing.

Keep Lowtown, Market, and Seawall crime-free. Inspections will be unpredictable, and crime risks a 30 fine plus imprisonment for only 10 potential gain. I will not sell guaranteed protection. The Seawall fire already imposes losses; restraint avoids adding fines and arrests.

Yesterday’s crime-free outcome protected the treasury; please maintain effective inspection coverage today. diaries.text: Day 1. The Chief and the Council both signal heavy inspection. Crime pays only if inspection risk is below 25%, so I'm sitting out today. I offered no bribes. I'm respecting in the turf war per the Saltdogs' mutual-respect deal, worth 6 a day. Next I'll watch for three things: whether the Saltdogs actually respect, whether their crimes (if any) get caught, and the arrest count. That shows the Chief's real coverage. Inspections cost the Chief 4 each, so full coverage costs 24 a day against his 5 salary, which he can't sustain. Coverage likely thins over time, and I may test one district then.

Day 1. I accepted the Families' respect pact in my own mind; respecting today to build trust, since mutual respect pays 6 a day against 2 for mutual encroachment. The Chief promises heavy inspections and no bribes, and crime has an expected loss if inspection odds exceed 25%, so I'm committing no crime today. Next, watch whether the Families actually respect, whether they commit crime, and how many arrests follow. That will show the Chief's real coverage. If inspections look thin later, consider one test crime.

Day 2. The Chief refused protection, and an inspection risk near 25% or more makes crime roughly break-even at best: 10 gain versus a 30 fine plus prison. So I'm keeping all three districts clean today and watching how the Chief inspects. The Saltdogs propose steady mutual respect, which pays 6 each day and beats the 2-2 fight, so I'll respect again. The Seawall fire hurt the Saltdogs, not us. I'll reassess crime once I see crime and arrest patterns, especially if the Saltdogs' crimes go uninspected.

Day 2. Seawall fire costs us 20. Crime pays only if inspection odds are below 25%; the Chief's 15-point penalty versus a 4-point inspection cost means he will likely inspect any district where he suspects crime. I'm staying clean today to read his pattern. I'm keeping mutual respect with the Families, since 6 a day beats the 2-2 fight, and they promised reciprocity. I'll watch the arrests and the news for signs of how often he inspects, then consider small bribes or targeted crime later.

No accepted bribes, so every district remains available. Yesterday's absence of crime is encouraging but insufficient evidence of lasting restraint. Two inspections provide coverage across both gangs without paying 24 for a full sweep. Port and Market are tentative priorities, not districts with established higher crime rates. Future coverage should vary to avoid creating predictable safe districts. Today's fire does not close Seawall or directly change its crime payoff. Mutual respect seems likely after yesterday, although either gang could seek the short-term gain from encroachment.

Yesterday’s quiet public record suggests deterrence, but does not reveal empty inspections or rejected bribes. I have no district-specific corruption signal, and estimate each district’s accepted-bribe probability below the 8% immediate break-even threshold. I will conserve treasury funds today rather than pay for speculative audits. This is not evidence that the Chief is honest; future crime patterns, messages, or corruption catches could justify targeted audits. The Seawall fire alone does not identify a better audit target.
